title: Audit escrow proxy for customer-owned sinks with resumable encrypted transfers
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Summary: Build an audit escrow proxy that enables Private/VPC/on-prem customers to forward audit records to customer-managed sinks (S3/GCS/Azure/compatible blobstores or on-prem object storage) using resumable, client-visible encrypted chunks. The escrow proxy acts as an optional staging layer inside the customer VPC or on-prem network that minimizes risk to Redwood while supporting tenant-level isolation, per-tenant retention policies, and customer KMS ownership.

Goals:
- Provide a reliable, resumable transfer mode for large audit batches and high-throughput streams without requiring customers to expose public endpoints.
- Support customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) handshake and resumable encrypted chunk uploads so that (a) Redwood never has plaintext copies, and (b) recovery/resume is possible after partial failures.
- Expose configurable routing policies (per-tenant mapping, multi-sink fanout, and fallback) to ensure durability and graceful degradation.
- Offer operator controls and observability hooks in Redwood Console for transfer progress, retry status, and retention reconciliation.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement of existing audit-forwarders; this is a complementary path for air-gapped or highly regulated customers who require escrow/staging in their network.

Design decisions (high-level):
- Proxy location: run a lightweight escrow proxy inside customer VPC or on-prem edge that accepts audit bundles over mTLS from Redwood, writes encrypted chunks to customer sink using signed, resumable multipart semantics (S3 multipart/GCS compose/azure block blobs or equivalent), and reports status to Redwood control-plane via an encrypted control channel.
- Encryption model: implement client-side envelope encryption. The customer KMS wraps data keys. The escrow proxy never stores the wrapped key unencrypted and stores only chunk metadata. Wrapped key handshake uses a short-lived signed metadata object in the sink root + control-plane verification.
- Resumable transfers: use chunk checksums + monotonic chunk indices persisted to a small local state store (SQLite) inside the proxy; on restart the proxy reconciles with sink object parts and resumes from last committed chunk.
- Tenant segmentation: metadata prefixes per-tenant + per-route ACLs enforced by proxy. Policy-driven routing allows fanout to multiple sinks and fallback to a cold-storage sink in case of primary failure.
- API surfaces: 1) Redwood->proxy gRPC stream for bundles, 2) proxy->Redwood control-plane REST callback for status, 3) minimal admin REST for operator actions (pause, resume, drain, list-resumable-uploads).

Security considerations:
- CMEK handshake: require customers to supply the wrapped data key location and KMS key ID in deployment manifest; validate signatures on handshake artifacts; ephemeral control-plane tokens for proxy authentication.
- Least privilege: use scoped signed URLs/service principals with minimal write permissions; rotate credentials on rollout; expose audit events for credential usage.
- Tamper evidence: chunk-level HMACs (derived from data key) stored in metadata; mismatches trigger reupload or alert.
- Compliance: preserve original audit record ordering by attaching sequence numbers and using monotonic sinks or ledger metadata.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Partial upload + proxy crash: resume using chunk index reconciliation and re-upload missing chunks; prevent double-commit via atomic finalize step (object rename or complete-multipart).
- Sink auth expiration: proxy rotates credentials and retries with backoff; alert to Redwood Console and customer operator email if rotation fails.
- Network partition (Redwood->proxy): Redwood will buffer up to configured retention in control-plane short-term queue and switch to fallback routing; Escrow proxy supports reconnection and will continue upload when available.

Deliverables / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement escrow proxy service with S3/GCS/Azure adapters, chunked encrypted multipart uploads, and SQLite local state persistence.
- Handshake protocol documented in Confluence and validated in security review.
- End-to-end demo: generate synthetic audit stream, forward through proxy to a customer S3 bucket using CMEK, simulate crash and resume, demonstrate no plaintext exposure in Redwood control-plane.
- Automated tests: unit coverage for chunk encryption/verification, integration tests for resume semantics against minio and GCS emulators, and e2e smoke in a private VPC test harness.
- Console telemetry: metrics for in-flight uploads, per-tenant backlog, failure rates, and final commit timestamps.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Alpha deploy to internal infra (minio) and run Canary for 2 customer staging tenants.
2) Security review + customer data-handling signoff.
3) Beta with selected customers using dedicated network segments.
4) GA as opt-in feature with docs and operator runbook.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- Whether to support server-side multipart for customers who cannot do client-side envelope encryption (trade-off: higher operator risk vs ease-of-use).
- How long to persist local state in proxy (disk vs ephemeral): choose a default 30 days TTL with admin purge.
- UX for customers to inspect chunk metadata in their sink vs via Redwood Console.

References and links:
